title: Greeting names one or two people, else Hello; invoice-style signature
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance. Open the schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', or create it with New schedule: add service 'PM-A' with a Calendar trigger of Every 6 months and canned lines, for example 'Engine oil and filter change' 0.8 hours, 'Chassis lubrication, 12 points' 0.5 hours, 'Air filter inspection' 0.3 hours and 'Brake adjustment check' 1.2 hours (4 lines, 2.8 hours). Save.
  3. Open Customers, open customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' (create it if missing), open its Assets tab and open unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' (create it with New Asset if missing). Open the asset's Maintenance tab. If the unit is not on the schedule, press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', enter a last service date for PM-A about seven months ago (for example 6 Mar 2026) and press Enroll. PM-A now reads Overdue on the Maintenance tab.
  4. Make sure 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' has its Send preventive maintenance notifications setting on, and a contact 'Dave Brabay' with an email address you can read (for example a QA mailbox) set as the preferred contact of unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402'.
  5. Give the customer two more contacts with email addresses you can read: 'Lisa Brabay' and 'Tom Brabay'.
  6. The location chosen in the header has a telephone number (for example 403-252-7710). A second location of the organization has no telephone (blank).
  7. On the QA environment, send only to a mailbox the QA team controls.
custom_steps:
1. Open Customers > Maintenance reminders (the worklist). On 402's row press Contact, then Send reminder. With only Dave Brabay ticked, read the greeting in Email content.
  2. Tick Lisa Brabay too and read the greeting.
  3. Tick Tom Brabay too and read the greeting.
  4. Untick Lisa and Tom, type another address in Optional emails, and read the greeting.
  5. Press Send. Open the email and read the greeting, the call to action and the signature.
  6. In the header choose the location with no telephone, send the reminder again, and read the email.
  7. In the sent email read the call to action word for word.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • One person ticked: the email opens Hi Dave Brabay,
  • Two people ticked: Hi Dave Brabay and Lisa Brabay,
  • Three or more ticked: Hello,
  • A typed address does not change the greeting: it stays Hi Dave Brabay,
  • The signature is the invoice email's: Best regards, your name, the organization's name and the header location's telephone (for example Northline Heavy Duty · 403-252-7710).
  • The call to action asks the customer to call.
  • From the location with no telephone, the call to action is left out rather than printed with nothing after it.
  • The call to action reads (in the design): “Give us a call and we will find a time that suits your schedule.”

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10575 (S19, The customer reminder email (sent by hand)); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S19; Design MR_V2_2 (Claude Design export, 6 Oct 2026), driven in full on 6 Oct 2026, Chunk 2 board artboard R1; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S19-R19: “The email opens with the first and last name of the person it goes to, for example Hi Dave Brabay. With two people ticked it names both, Hi Dave Brabay and Lisa Brabay; with three or more, or where no ticked address carries a name, it reads Hello. The signature is the one the invoice email already carries: Best regards, the user's name, the organization's name and the telephone of the location chosen in the header. The call to action is to call. Booking is a conversation, and a telephone is present where an email address often is not. An address typed in the dialog's field does not change the greeting”
  • S19-R21: “Where the location has no telephone, the call to action is omitted rather than printed with nothing after it”
  • Design, Chunk 2 board, artboard R1, email body: “Give us a call and we will find a time that suits your schedule.”
